name: Lens Grime
desc: The dirt on the front element, which stays invisible until something bright rakes it — a glare source wanders the frame and wakes what it passes: sleeve-wipe arcs, a thumbprint whorl, hairline scratches flaring out of nowhere, dust flecks lighting up, and a veiling haze blooming around the source.

soil.doc: how dirty the front element is — 0 = clean glass, 1.2 = never once wiped

scale.doc: size of the marks — how close the grime sits to the front element

energy.doc: how brightly the glare source wakes the grime it passes

density.doc: how many smears, scratches and flecks there are, and the reach of the glare

hue.doc: tint of the coating bloom under the grime

speed.doc: how fast the glare source wanders the frame

x.doc: where the glare source sits, across the frame

y.doc: where the glare source sits, up the frame

alpha.doc: overlay opacity — kept off full by default so this veils the scene rather than hiding it

style.doc: grime: general lens crud — sleeve smears, flecks and a veiling haze · fingerprint: someone put a thumb on the front element, whorls and all · scratched: cleaned once too often with the wrong cloth, hairlines everywhere · bloom: the coating has gone — a soft flaring haze with almost no marks · survey: non-representational — an optical QC plot, every defect ringed and ticked on a clean field, nothing rendered as material at all

act.doc: drift: the glare source wanders and wakes what it passes · wipe: someone drags a cloth across — the smears sweep round and thin out · fog: the coating blooms, haze swelling and receding across sections

seed.doc: a different lens — new smears, prints, scratches and flecks
